docs.title: Related projects
docs.text: PyroApp is part of a larger set of thermodynamic and scientific-software projects.

docs.title: chemsage-parser
docs.text: A Rust parser/editor for open ChemSage/ChemApp DAT files. PyroApp uses it for local LIST/GET/SET operations, including model-aware interaction identity and transactional parameter edits.

docs.title: chemapp_rs
docs.text: Rust bindings and safe ownership wrappers around the native ChemApp library. PyroApp worker processes use this layer for thermodynamic execution.

docs.title: chemapp_parallel
docs.text: A Rust batch-calculation project that demonstrates thread-affine ChemApp worker ownership and dynamic scheduling for strongly uneven calculation costs. Its dynamic work-claim model is a design precedent for PyroApp server scheduling.

docs.title: Legacy PyroApp
docs.text:
The Python/xlwings project defines the original worksheet workflows and remains a useful compatibility reference while PyroApp is completed.

These developer projects are implementation dependencies/references. A normal PyroApp user does not need to install them separately when using an approved release package.

docs.title: Runtime transport controls
docs.text: Transport controls select where ChemApp runtime work, especially XLL_CA_CALCULATE, executes. DAT LIST/GET/SET functions remain local regardless of this setting.

docs.title: Show the active transport
docs.text:
=XLL_PYROAPP_TRANSPORT()

Returns IPC or gRPC according to the active process configuration.

docs.title: Configure the connection
docs.text:
Use the PyroApp Ribbon tab's Connection group. Choose Local (IPC) or Remote (gRPC); for remote mode enter the http:// or https:// server address, use Test Connection, then choose Apply.

Local IPC uses the ChemApp worker on the same computer as Excel. It can use either the fixed runtime from a controlled bundled PyroApp installation or an explicitly configured external runtime. Remote gRPC sends XLL_CA_CALCULATE work to the selected server.

The setting applies to the whole Excel/PyroApp process, is saved per user in %LOCALAPPDATA%\PyroApp\settings.json, and never changes a workbook. Applying a new destination changes the asynchronous execution identity of subsequent runtime formulas.

docs.title: Transport and runtime packaging are independent
docs.text:
Transport answers where calculation work runs; packaging answers where a local worker finds ChemApp. They are separate choices:

Calculation path Local ChemApp requirement Local IPC + bundled package The worker uses the installed PyroApp ChemApp directory. Environment/PATH discovery is not used. Local IPC + external package The worker uses the configured licensed external runtime. Remote gRPC The remote server provides ChemApp; a local ChemApp runtime is not required for that calculation path.

docs.title: Compatibility formulas
docs.text:
XLL_PYROAPP_USE_IPC() and XLL_PYROAPP_USE_GRPC(...) remain registered so legacy workbooks open, but they are deprecated and do not change the connection. XLL_PYROAPP_GRPC_ADDRESS() returns the configured address; its optional legacy argument is ignored.

Read it:

=XLL_PYROAPP_GRPC_ADDRESS()

Scope

The Ribbon configures the current Excel/PyroApp process. It is not a thermodynamic condition and does not alter the contents of a DAT file.

Network access

A non-local gRPC endpoint must be configured and authorized by the server operator. Do not expose a PyroApp server to an untrusted network merely by binding it to all interfaces.

docs.title: System units
docs.text:
XLL_CA_CALCULATE accepts optional unit declarations in the first row of an input or output header. Use this form:

CODE, [unit]

Examples:

T, [C]
P, [kPa]
H, [kJ is not supported]

Only the units listed below are accepted. Each column is interpreted independently; omitting a unit restores that family's documented default rather than inheriting the preceding column's setting.

Quantity Default Accepted units Temperature K K, C, F Pressure bar bar, atm, Pa, kPa, psi, torr Amount mol mol, gram, kg, tonne, pound Energy J J, cal, Btu, kWh Volume dm3 dm3, cm3, m3, ft3, in3

Multiple unit families can be associated with a property where ChemApp requires them. Write the units inside the bracket list separated by commas.

Tip

Use defaults while learning PyroApp. Add explicit units only where a workbook needs a different engineering convention, such as T, [C].

Warning

Unit spellings are part of the calculation interface. Do not assume arbitrary SI prefixes are accepted. For example, use one of the pressure units in the table rather than inventing MPa unless the current function documentation explicitly adds it.

docs.title: The functions do not appear in Excel
docs.text: Confirm that you loaded the packed XLL matching Excel bitness. If you replaced the package while Excel was running, close all Excel processes and reopen the workbook.

docs.title: #SPILL!
docs.text: A PyroApp array needs empty cells below/right of the formula. Clear the obstructing values or move the formula.

docs.title: DAT function reports “unsupported datafile format”
docs.text: LIST/GET/SET parameter functions in PyroApp use the local open-DAT parser. They require .DAT. Protected .CST parameter inspection/editing is intentionally unsupported. Use CST only for ChemApp calculation where your licence permits it.

docs.title: DAT parsing failed
docs.text: The local parser uses strict DAT parsing. Verify that the file is complete and is genuinely a ChemSage/ChemApp DAT file. If you hand-edited it, compare it with the last known working revision.

docs.title: Entity not found
docs.text: Use the LIST functions rather than guessing names. Phase, constituent and interaction identities must match the datafile.

docs.title: A SET function changed the database
docs.text: That is expected: current SET functions modify the canonical DAT file at the path. Restore the file from version control/backup if the change was not intended.

docs.title: Local CA_CALCULATE cannot load ChemApp
docs.text:
Run PyroApp diagnostic from the Start menu first. It reports whether the installed package expects a bundled or external runtime and validates the architecture.

  • Bundled runtime expected: pyroapp.runtime.json must identify bundled, and chemapp_00.dll must exist under the installed PyroApp ChemApp directory. Do not set PYROAPP_CHEMAPP_HOME to try to redirect a bundled package.
  • External runtime expected: configure PYROAPP_CHEMAPP_HOME or pyroapp.runtime.json with the existing licensed runtime folder containing chemapp_00.dll.

In both modes, the worker and ChemApp DLLs must match the Excel bitness. PyroApp loads ChemApp in an isolated worker rather than Excel, so do not register ChemApp DLLs in Excel.

docs.title: The installer says Excel bitness does not match
docs.text: Open File → Account → About Excel and use the installer with the same bitness. Windows bitness is not the deciding factor; Excel's bitness is.

docs.title: The external installer cannot find ChemApp
docs.text: This applies only to an ExternalChemApp installer. Browse to the existing licensed runtime directory containing chemapp_00.dll. Contact the ChemApp supplier if you do not have a compatible runtime and licence. A bundled installer does not show this page; it still requires a valid ChemApp licence to calculate.

docs.title: The installer says that .NET Desktop Runtime is required
docs.text: Install Microsoft .NET Desktop Runtime 8.x matching the PyroApp/Excel architecture, then rerun the installer. A developer SDK, Visual Studio, Cargo, or a source checkout is not required.

docs.title: A worker remains after Excel closed
docs.text: Workers are owned by the XLL and also monitor the Excel process. If a process persists, record the PyroApp version, diagnostic output, and process ID before ending it, then report it as a defect. Do not delete the installed folder while Excel is running.

docs.title: A remote calculation cannot connect
docs.text:
Check:

=XLL_PYROAPP_TRANSPORT()
=XLL_PYROAPP_GRPC_ADDRESS()

Verify the server name/port with the operator. The server must be configured to listen on an address reachable from your machine.

To change the endpoint, use PyroApp → Connection in the Ribbon, then Test Connection and Apply. The worksheet compatibility formulas do not change the process-wide connection.

docs.title: Some calculation rows are NaN
docs.text: Add an ERROR column to the output header. Point-level ChemApp failures can allow the rest of the table to continue. Check target limits, phase selection, units and whether the calculation is thermodynamically well constrained.

docs.title: Results look off by a unit factor
docs.text: Each header column has its own units. Explicitly write the unit in row 1 (for example T, [C]) and check the System units table. PyroApp does not inherit a custom unit from the previous column.

docs.title: Excel does not recalculate after I changed a DAT file externally
docs.text: Change the formula's update_token. Excel tracks cell dependencies, not arbitrary file contents.

docs.title: XLL_BEST_COMBINATION
docs.text:
Status: implemented optimization helper.

Searches combinations of adjustable parameters and identifies the subset that performs best under the legacy linear-regression objective.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_BEST_COMBINATION(derivatives,residuals,weight,free,fixed_values,nparams)

nparams is the number of parameters to include in each candidate combination. Other arguments follow XLL_LINEAR_REGRESSION.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
An integer vector identifying the selected parameter combination.

The search can be combinatorial; use it only on a deliberately limited candidate set.

docs.title: XLL_CA_CALCULATE
docs.text: XLL_CA_CALCULATE is PyroApp's main equilibrium function. One formula describes a complete table of ChemApp calculations and returns one output row for every input row.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_CALCULATE(datafile,input_header,input,output_header,[entered],[update_token])

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Meaning datafile Absolute or workbook-relative ChemApp datafile path. DAT/CST/BIN calculation formats are supported according to the configured ChemApp runtime. input_header 3 × N block: code/unit, phase, constituent/component. Use ="" for unused phase/component cells. input R × N block: R calculation points using the columns described by input_header. output_header 3 × M block: code/unit, phase, constituent/component. Use ="" for unused phase/component cells. entered Optional phase-selection block. See Phase selection below. update_token Optional arbitrary dependency value used to force recalculation when an external file changes.

docs.title: The three-row header
docs.text:
Both input and output headers use the same shape:

Header row Meaning 1 condition/property code, optionally followed by units, e.g. T, [C] 2 phase name when phase-specific; otherwise the default value "" (enter ="" in a worksheet cell) 3 phase constituent or system component when needed; otherwise the default value "" (enter ="" in a worksheet cell)

The phase and constituent/component header rows should never use genuinely empty cells as defaults. When a field does not apply, the worksheet cell must contain ="", which evaluates to the runtime value "".

This convention keeps the three-row header fully populated as a contiguous table, which makes it much easier to select, copy, resize, filter, and manipulate in Excel.

docs.title: Example layout
docs.text:
Suppose B1 contains the datafile path. The input header is B4:E6, input points are B7:E106, and the output header is G4:J6:

=XLL_CA_CALCULATE($B$1,B4:E6,B7:E106,G4:J6)

The result spills as a 100 × 4 matrix.

See First equilibrium for a complete example and Input conditions / Output properties for the code tables.

docs.title: Phase selection
docs.text:
The optional entered argument supplies a base phase selection.

  • A one-row range containing phase names marks those phases entered.
  • A two-or-more-row range can pair phase names with status prefixes EN, D, or EL for entered, dormant, or eliminated status.

Row-local ENTERED, DORMANT and ELIMINATED input columns are applied after the base selection, so they can vary the selection from point to point.

docs.title: Target calculations
docs.text:
A target condition asks ChemApp to solve for a variable rather than simply evaluate a fixed T/P state. Target-triggering inputs include A, CP, H, S, G, V, AT, XP, XPT, FORMATION, and PRECIPITATION.

The default target variable is temperature. VARIABLE can select T, P, V, IA, or IA0 where appropriate. Search limits can be supplied using TLOW/THIGH, PLOW/PHIGH, or VLOW/VHIGH.

docs.title: Row independence
docs.text: Current PyroApp rejects the legacy USEFORNEXT control. It would make a row depend on whichever row executed immediately before it, which is incompatible with reliable dynamic scheduling of independent points.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Malformed headers or unknown names fail the formula. Some native ChemApp calculation errors are treated as point-level failures so other rows can continue. Add an ERROR output column to retrieve the current row's native error code; a successful row reports 0.

NSTABLE counts phases whose activity is strictly greater than 0.9999.

docs.title: Transport behavior
docs.text:
• IPC: the local worker opens the original client path.
  • gRPC: PyroApp synchronizes the exact datafile version to the server cache, then the server schedules ChemApp work.

This is the only normal PyroApp datafile operation that uploads a file to the remote server.

docs.title: XLL_CA_CHEMAPPDLLS
docs.text:
Availability: stable runtime diagnostic.

Returns the ChemApp native-library paths/specifications visible to the selected runtime implementation.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_CHEMAPPDLLS([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A one-column dynamic array of library paths or loader specifications.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_CHEMAPPDLLS()

This is mainly a configuration/troubleshooting function. Do not edit, rename, or replace licensed native libraries simply to change this output. Local IPC and remote gRPC can describe different runtime environments.

See ChemApp and licensing and Runtime transport controls.

docs.title: XLL_CA_COPYRIGHT
docs.text:
Availability: stable.

Returns the copyright message reported by the selected ChemApp runtime.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_COPYRIGHT([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A text value.

This function is informational and does not load or inspect a thermodynamic datafile.

docs.title: XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns structural counts from an open ChemSage/ChemApp DAT file. Unlike the runtime information functions, this operation is handled by the local DAT parser and is unaffected by IPC/gRPC selection.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS(datafile,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A two-column spill range containing the current parser-exposed counts:

  • number_system_components
  • number_phases
  • number_phase_constituents

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS($B$1)

.CST and .BIN are not supported by this inspection function. Use XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS_MAX for native runtime limits.

docs.title: XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS_MAX
docs.text:
Availability: stable runtime diagnostic.

Returns ChemApp capacity/dimension information for the selected runtime.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS_MAX([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A two-column spill range: dimension name and maximum value.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS_MAX()

For the dimensions actually occupied by an open DAT file, use XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS.

docs.title: XLL_CA_DONGLE_INFO
docs.text:
Availability: stable.

Returns information reported for the ChemApp licence dongle/runtime entitlement.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_DONGLE_INFO([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A horizontal two-cell array containing the reported dongle name/description and dongle identifier.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_DONGLE_INFO()

The exact text depends on the installed/licensed ChemApp runtime.

docs.title: XLL_CA_EXPIRATION_DATE
docs.text:
Availability: stable.

Returns the licence expiration information reported by the selected ChemApp runtime.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_EXPIRATION_DATE([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A horizontal two-cell array: month and year.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_EXPIRATION_DATE()

The meaning of a particular returned date is controlled by the ChemApp licence/provider, not by PyroApp.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_COMPONENT_STOICHIOMETRY
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns selected system components expressed in the complete system-component basis of the DAT file.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_GET_COMPONENT_STOICHIOMETRY(datafile,components,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A matrix with one row per requested component and one column per component in the DAT basis. For an existing system component this is the corresponding unit-basis row; a missing requested name produces a NaN row.

This function is useful when constructing generic composition-processing workbooks that need an explicit basis matrix.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_COMPONENT_WEIGHTS
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns molar masses for selected system components.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_GET_COMPONENT_WEIGHTS(datafile,components,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A one-column numeric array in the same order as components, in the molar-mass units stored by the DAT format (normally g/mol for ChemSage/ChemApp component declarations). A component name not found in the DAT is returned as NaN.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_COMPONENT_WEIGHTS($B$1,D2:D5)

Use XLL_CA_LIST_COMPONENTS to obtain valid component names.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_CP
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Reads thermochemical coefficient data for selected compound ranges. The historical function name says CP; the exact physical interpretation of the stored coefficient vector depends on the DAT thermochemical representation.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_CP(datafile,phases,range_indices,value_indices,[update_token])
  • range_indices are one-based.
  • value_indices are 1..10 for one displayed coefficient, or 0 to return the complete ten-coefficient display vector for the corresponding range.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A numeric matrix. The safest rectangular usage is to request the same coefficient mode for every target (all 0, or one indexed coefficient per target).

PyroApp maps the ten public coefficient positions to the correct DAT source fields; callers should use the public 1..10 ordering rather than physical record offsets.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_H298
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns the stored standard enthalpy at 298 K for selected stoichiometric compound phases.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_H298(datafile,phases,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: One numeric value per requested phase. If the compound exists but its thermochemical representation does not directly contain an H298 value, PyroApp returns NaN rather than inventing one from a different representation.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_H298($B$1,D2:D8)

This function reads the DAT locally through chemsage-parser; it does not call ChemApp TQGDAT and does not support CST.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_RANGE_COUNT
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns the number of thermochemical temperature ranges/intervals stored for each selected stoichiometric compound.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_RANGE_COUNT(datafile,phases,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A one-column integer array, one count per phase.

Use the returned count to validate the one-based range_indices supplied to XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_TUPPER, XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_CP, or the corresponding SET function.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_S298
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns the stored standard entropy at 298 K for selected stoichiometric compounds.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_S298(datafile,phases,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
One numeric value per requested phase. NaN indicates that the requested value is not directly available from the compound's stored thermochemical representation.

Use XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_H298, XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_RANGE_COUNT, and XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_CP for the related standard-state fields.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_STOICHIOMETRY
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns selected compound compositions in the DAT system-component basis.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_STOICHIOMETRY(datafile,phases,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A matrix with one row per requested compound and one column per system component, in the same component order returned by XLL_CA_LIST_COMPONENTS. A missing compound yields a NaN row.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_TUPPER
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns the upper temperature associated with a selected thermochemical range for each compound.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_TUPPER(datafile,phases,ranges,[update_token])

ranges contains one-based range indices corresponding to the requested phases.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
One upper-temperature value per phase/range pair.

Use XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_RANGE_COUNT first when the valid range count is not known.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_WEIGHTS
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Calculates molar masses of selected stoichiometric compound phases from their DAT stoichiometry and component molar masses.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_GET_COMPOUND_WEIGHTS(datafile,phases,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
One numeric molar mass per requested compound. A missing compound returns NaN.

Use XLL_CA_LIST_COMPOUNDS to obtain valid names.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_CP
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Reads thermochemical coefficient data for selected solution-phase constituents.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_CP(datafile,phases,constituents,range_indices,value_indices,[update_token])

phases and constituents identify paired targets. range_indices are one-based. A value_index of 1..10 selects one public coefficient; 0 returns the full ten-coefficient display vector for that target/range.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A numeric matrix. NaN can appear where a requested coefficient is not structurally available from the stored representation.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_H298
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns stored standard enthalpies at 298 K for solution-phase constituents/endmembers.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_H298(datafile,phases,constituents,[update_token])

phases and constituents are paired arrays and must have equal lengths.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
One value per (phase,constituent) pair. A value that is not directly represented in the DAT is returned as NaN.

Use XLL_CA_LIST_CONSTITUENTS to obtain valid constituent names.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_RANGE_COUNT
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns the number of thermochemical temperature ranges stored for selected solution-phase constituents.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_RANGE_COUNT(datafile,phases,constituents,[update_token])

phases and constituents are paired arrays.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: One integer range count per requested constituent.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_S298
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns stored standard entropies at 298 K for solution-phase constituents/endmembers.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_S298(datafile,phases,constituents,[update_token])

phases and constituents are paired arrays of equal length.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: One value per requested pair. NaN means that the value is not directly available in the stored thermochemical representation.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_STOICHIOMETRY
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns selected phase-constituent compositions in the DAT system-component basis.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_STOICHIOMETRY(datafile,phases,constituents,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A matrix with one row per (phase,constituent) pair and one column per system component, ordered as XLL_CA_LIST_COMPONENTS.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_TUPPER
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Returns the upper temperature associated with a selected thermochemical range for each phase constituent.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_TUPPER(datafile,phases,constituents,ranges,[update_token])

phases, constituents, and ranges describe corresponding targets; range indices are one-based.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: One upper-temperature value per target.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_WEIGHTS
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Calculates molar masses for selected phase constituents from their component-basis stoichiometry.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_CONSTITUENT_WEIGHTS(datafile,phases,constituents,[update_token])

The phase and constituent arrays are paired.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: One numeric molar mass per pair.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_INTERACTION_INDICES
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Resolves ordinary interaction descriptions to their positional identities in the parsed phase model.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_INTERACTION_INDICES(datafile,phases,interactions,[update_token])

phases and interactions are paired arrays and must have equal lengths.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
One integer interaction position per requested pair.

Tip

Generate the interactions input with XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_G. Do not reconstruct interaction text manually, particularly when powers are greater than 9.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_INTERACTIONS_PARAMETERS_G
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Reads the fixed thermodynamic coefficients of ordinary excess-Gibbs interaction records.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_INTERACTIONS_PARAMETERS_G(datafile,phases,interactions,value_indices,[update_token])

phases and interactions are paired. value_indices selects coefficients:

Index Term 0 return all six terms 1 constant 2 linear in T 3 T·ln(T) 4 T² 5 T³ 6 1/T

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A matrix of requested interaction coefficient values.

Interaction descriptions come from the DAT parser rather than TQLPAR, so multi-digit interaction powers are preserved correctly.

docs.title: XLL_CA_GET_INTERACTIONS_PARAMETERS_M
docs.text:
Availability: stable for magnetic interaction families exposed by the current DAT parser.

Reads magnetic interaction parameters for selected interactions.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_GET_INTERACTIONS_PARAMETERS_M(datafile,phases,interactions,[update_token])

phases and interactions are paired arrays.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
One row per interaction. For each magnetic expression, values are returned as alternating pairs:

Tcrit_1, beta_1, Tcrit_2, beta_2, ...

The number of expressions is model/record dependent.

Use XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_M to obtain the interaction identities accepted by this function.

docs.title: XLL_CA_ISLITE
docs.text:
Availability: stable.

Reports whether the selected ChemApp runtime identifies itself as a Lite/demo-capability library.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_ISLITE([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: TRUE or FALSE.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_ISLITE()

This is a runtime property, not a property of a DAT file.

docs.title: XLL_CA_LICENSE_HOLDER_NAME
docs.text:
Availability: stable.

Returns the licence-holder name reported by the selected ChemApp runtime.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_LICENSE_HOLDER_NAME([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A text value.

Use together with XLL_CA_USER_ID, XLL_CA_DONGLE_INFO, and XLL_CA_EXPIRATION_DATE when diagnosing a protected database or workstation setup.

docs.title: XLL_CA_LIST_COMPONENTS
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Lists the system components declared by a ChemSage/ChemApp DAT file, in datafile order.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_LIST_COMPONENTS(datafile,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A one-column dynamic array of component names.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_LIST_COMPONENTS($B$1)

Use the returned spelling when constructing IA, XP, or other component-addressed XLL_CA_CALCULATE headers. This function parses the DAT locally and never uploads the file.

docs.title: XLL_CA_LIST_COMPOUNDS
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Lists fixed-composition (stoichiometric) compound phases.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_LIST_COMPOUNDS(datafile,[system],[update_token])

system optionally limits results to compounds representable in the supplied chemical basis.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A one-column dynamic array of compound phase names.

Use XLL_CA_LIST_SOLUTIONS for variable-composition phases.

docs.title: XLL_CA_LIST_CONSTITUENTS
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Lists phase constituents/endmembers for one or more solution phases.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_LIST_CONSTITUENTS(datafile,phases,[system],[update_token])

system optionally filters constituents by chemical basis. Results for multiple phases are appended sequentially.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A one-column dynamic array of constituent names.

Use these exact names in constituent-addressed GET functions or in XLL_CA_CALCULATE header row 3.

docs.title: XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_G
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Lists ordinary (non-magnetic) interaction descriptions for the requested solution phases.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_G(datafile,phases,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A one-column spill range of stable interaction descriptions derived from the parsed DAT model.

Use the returned descriptions

Pass these values directly to interaction GET/SET functions. PyroApp does not use ChemApp TQLPAR display strings as interaction identity because native formatting can misrepresent powers greater than 9. Multi-digit powers are preserved by the DAT parser.

For magnetic interactions use XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_M.

docs.title: XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_M
docs.text:
Availability: stable for model families exposed by the current DAT parser.

Lists magnetic interaction participants for the requested solution phases.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_M(datafile,phases,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A one-column spill range of parser-derived magnetic interaction identities/descriptions.

Use these values as the interactions argument of XLL_CA_GET_INTERACTIONS_PARAMETERS_M and XLL_CA_SET_INTERACTION_PARAMETERS_M rather than reconstructing names manually.

This is an open-DAT operation; CST parameter inspection is not supported.

docs.title: XLL_CA_LIST_PHASES
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Lists both solution phases and stoichiometric compounds in the DAT file.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_LIST_PHASES(datafile,[system],[update_token])
Argument Meaning datafile Open .DAT path. system Optional chemical-system filter such as Ca-Si-O or Na2O-Al2O3-SiO2. update_token Optional recalculation dependency.

The system filter keeps phases whose declared stoichiometry can be represented inside the supplied chemical basis. Leave it blank to list all phases.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A one-column spill range of phase names.

See Common definitions.

docs.title: XLL_CA_LIST_SOLUTIONS
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Lists variable-composition solution/mixture phases.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_LIST_SOLUTIONS(datafile,[system],[update_token])

system is an optional chemical-system filter. Leave it blank to return every solution phase in datafile order.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A one-column dynamic array of solution phase names.

For fixed-composition phases use XLL_CA_LIST_COMPOUNDS; for both categories use XLL_CA_LIST_PHASES.

docs.title: XLL_CA_LIST_SPECIES
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Lists the sublattice species declared for one or more solution phases.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_LIST_SPECIES(datafile,phases,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A two-column spill range:

  1. species name;
  2. one-based sublattice number.

Species from the requested phases are appended in request/datafile order.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_LIST_SPECIES($B$1,D2:D3)

A species is not always the same thing as a phase constituent. See Common definitions.

docs.title: XLL_CA_PROGRAM_ID
docs.text:
Availability: stable.

Returns the program identifier reported by the selected ChemApp runtime.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_PROGRAM_ID([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A text value suitable for runtime diagnostics.

docs.title: XLL_CA_SET_COMPOUND_CP
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Changes thermochemical coefficients for selected compound ranges.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_SET_COMPOUND_CP(datafile,phases,range_indices,value_indices,values,[update_token])

For every target phase supply one one-based range_index and one value_index.

  • value_index = 1..10: the corresponding row of values supplies that public coefficient.
  • value_index = 0: the corresponding values row must contain exactly ten coefficients and replaces the full public coefficient vector for that range.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
One Boolean status per phase/edit row.

Warning

The historical CP name covers the DAT thermochemical coefficient vector. The physical interpretation depends on the record representation. Inspect the original values and range structure before editing.

docs.title: XLL_CA_SET_COMPOUND_H298
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Changes the stored H298 value for selected stoichiometric compounds.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_SET_COMPOUND_H298(datafile,phases,values,[update_token])

phases and values must describe corresponding targets.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A Boolean status array, one value per requested edit.

This edits the DAT file

The canonical file at datafile is replaced atomically after parsing, semantic validation and serialization succeed. Keep a backup or use version control before changing thermodynamic parameters.

The function is local even when gRPC calculation transport is selected.

docs.title: XLL_CA_SET_COMPOUND_S298
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Changes stored S298 values for selected stoichiometric compounds.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_SET_COMPOUND_S298(datafile,phases,values,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A Boolean status array corresponding to the requested phases.

The DAT file is edited at the supplied path using a validated transactional update. If the requested representation cannot store the parameter safely, the edit fails rather than inventing a new thermodynamic representation.

docs.title: XLL_CA_SET_CONSTITUENT_CP
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Changes thermochemical coefficients for solution-phase constituents.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_SET_CONSTITUENT_CP(datafile,phases,constituents,range_indices,value_indices,values,[update_token])

Each target has a paired phase, constituent, one-based range index and coefficient index. value_index = 1..10 edits one public coefficient; 0 requires a complete ten-value row.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A Boolean status array.

The edit is semantic and transactional; PyroApp does not patch DAT text by position.

docs.title: XLL_CA_SET_CONSTITUENT_H298
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Changes stored H298 values for selected solution-phase constituents/endmembers.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_SET_CONSTITUENT_H298(datafile,phases,constituents,values,[update_token])

phases, constituents, and values are corresponding arrays.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
One Boolean status per requested edit.

The operation modifies the DAT at the same path only after the complete semantic edit validates successfully.

docs.title: XLL_CA_SET_CONSTITUENT_S298
docs.text:
Availability: stable, open-DAT only.

Changes stored S298 values for selected solution-phase constituents/endmembers.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_SET_CONSTITUENT_S298(datafile,phases,constituents,values,[update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A Boolean status array.

Use XLL_CA_LIST_CONSTITUENTS to obtain exact constituent names. This is a local parser/editor operation; it does not call ChemApp or upload the DAT.

docs.title: XLL_CA_SET_INTERACTION_PARAMETERS_G
docs.text:
Availability: stable for ordinary interaction terms exposed by the current DAT parser.

Changes one fixed thermodynamic term for each selected ordinary excess-Gibbs interaction.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_SET_INTERACTION_PARAMETERS_G(datafile,phases,interactions,value_indices,values,[update_token])

phases, interactions, value_indices, and values correspond by position.

Value index Term 1 constant 2 linear in T 3 T·ln(T) 4 T² 5 T³ 6 1/T

Use XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_G to obtain exact interaction descriptions.

Important

Interaction identity comes from chemsage-parser, not TQLPAR display text, so powers above 9 remain unambiguous.

The DAT is atomically updated at the supplied path.

docs.title: XLL_CA_SET_INTERACTION_PARAMETERS_M
docs.text:
Availability: stable for magnetic interaction families exposed by the current DAT parser.

Changes magnetic interaction parameters in a local DAT file.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_SET_INTERACTION_PARAMETERS_M(datafile,phases,interactions,values,[update_token])

phases and interactions identify corresponding targets. values supports two useful layouts:

  • one value per interaction — changes the first expression's critical temperature (Tcrit);
  • complete flattened expression data — for each interaction supply Tcrit, beta pairs for every magnetic expression in that record.

Use XLL_CA_GET_INTERACTIONS_PARAMETERS_M first to see the expression width for a record.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A Boolean status array.

The edit is validated and written atomically to the original DAT path.

docs.title: XLL_CA_USER_ID
docs.text:
Availability: stable.

Returns the user identifier reported by the selected ChemApp runtime/licence environment.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_USER_ID([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A text value.

This value can matter when a protected CST database is licensed to a particular ChemApp/FactSage user environment. PyroApp does not alter or bypass that restriction.

docs.title: XLL_CA_VERSION
docs.text:
Availability: stable.

Returns the ChemApp version reported by the selected runtime.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: =XLL_CA_VERSION([update_token])

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A numeric ChemApp version value as reported by the native library.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_VERSION()

Use this when checking that a workbook is running against the expected local worker or remote server runtime. The function does not inspect a DAT file.

docs.title: XLL_DATA_CHANGE_BASIS
docs.text:
Availability: stable utility in the current PyroApp interface.

Converts composition rows from one independent chemical-formula basis to another, optionally converting between mole and mass bases and optionally normalizing the result.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_DATA_CHANGE_BASIS(basis_initial,basis_final,data_initial,[isweight_initial],[isweight_final],[is_fraction])
Argument Meaning basis_initial Formula units describing columns of data_initial. basis_final Desired output formula basis. data_initial Rows of compositions/amounts. isweight_initial TRUE if the input values are a mass/weight basis; default FALSE. isweight_final TRUE for a mass/weight output basis; default FALSE. is_fraction TRUE to normalize each output row to sum to one; default FALSE.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A composition matrix in basis_final order.

Example bases can contain formula units such as CaO, SiO2, FeO, or elements, provided the transformation is chemically well-defined.

docs.title: XLL_DATA_GENERATE_MESH
docs.text:
Status: implemented data utility.

The legacy function generates a uniform composition mesh for a chosen number of active and total components.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_DATA_GENERATE_MESH(nintervals,nactive,ntotal)
Argument Meaning nintervals Number of composition intervals used to discretize the active simplex. nactive Number of composition components that vary. ntotal Total number of output composition components, including non-varying/padded components.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A matrix of composition-grid points.

docs.title: XLL_DATA_REPEAT
docs.text:
Status: implemented data utility.

The legacy utility repeats input rows/elements according to requested repeat counts. It is useful for expanding compact design tables into repeated calculation blocks.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_DATA_REPEAT(values,times)

values is a two-dimensional range. times supplies the repeat count(s).

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: An expanded matrix containing repeated input entries/rows according to the legacy utility contract.

docs.title: XLL_INTERACTIONS_SYSTEM_COUNT
docs.text:
XLL_INTERACTIONS_SYSTEM_COUNT(legacy_chemapp_dll, datafile, phase, systems) counts ordinary excess-Gibbs interaction declarations whose participant element set exactly matches each requested system.

The first argument is retained only for legacy workbook compatibility and is ignored. datafile must be an open ASCII DAT file, phase is a mixture phase, and systems is a vertical or horizontal range of dash-separated systems such as Cu-S and Cu-Fe-S.

The function uses the local parser-backed DAT boundary. It does not start ChemApp or use the selected calculation transport.

docs.title: XLL_LINEAR_REGRESSION
docs.text:
Status: implemented continuous-optimization helper.

The legacy function calculates parameter corrections from a derivative matrix using a weighted linear approximation. It is intended for iterative thermodynamic assessment workflows.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_LINEAR_REGRESSION(derivatives,residuals,weight,free,fixed_values)
  • derivatives: N×K sensitivity/derivative matrix for N targets and K parameters.
  • residuals: target-minus-calculated (or the workflow's defined residual) vector.
  • weight: point weights.
  • free: Boolean vector selecting adjustable parameters.
  • fixed_values: static/frozen parameter contributions.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A parameter-correction vector according to the legacy optimization convention.

docs.title: XLL_PD_ERROR_TABLE
docs.text:
Status: implemented optimization/reporting helper.

Builds a compact residual-statistics table for categories of experimental/target points, comparing two residual vectors.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
=XLL_PD_ERROR_TABLE(categories,residuals1,residuals2,mask,dTdx)

The legacy result summarizes quantities such as point count, mean/RMS error, minima and maxima by category and overall. mask selects included points; dTdx carries an optional derivative/scaling vector used by the phase-diagram error workflow.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: A table whose first column contains category labels and remaining columns contain statistics.

docs.title: ChemApp runtime information
docs.text:
PyroApp exposes several formulas that query the selected ChemApp runtime and licence environment.

Useful checks include:

=XLL_CA_VERSION()
=XLL_CA_ISLITE()
=XLL_CA_USER_ID()
=XLL_CA_LICENSE_HOLDER_NAME()
=XLL_CA_PROGRAM_ID()
=XLL_CA_DONGLE_INFO()
=XLL_CA_EXPIRATION_DATE()

XLL_CA_DONGLE_INFO returns two cells (a name/description and dongle identifier). XLL_CA_EXPIRATION_DATE returns month and year fields.

These functions are particularly useful before troubleshooting a protected CST file: a CST file may be tied to a particular user/licence environment.

XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS_MAX() reports ChemApp runtime capacity information. XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS(datafile) is different in the current client: it is a local DAT query and reports structural counts from an open DAT file.

When gRPC is selected, runtime information is associated with the configured runtime path/server implementation rather than the local DAT parser.

docs.title: Working with DAT files
docs.text: Open .DAT files are the inspectable/editable database format in PyroApp.

docs.title: Discover the datafile
docs.text:
Start with:

=XLL_CA_LIST_COMPONENTS(datafile)
=XLL_CA_LIST_PHASES(datafile)
=XLL_CA_LIST_SOLUTIONS(datafile)
=XLL_CA_LIST_COMPOUNDS(datafile)

For a solution phase, inspect:

=XLL_CA_LIST_CONSTITUENTS(datafile,phases)
=XLL_CA_LIST_SPECIES(datafile,phases)
=XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_G(datafile,phases)
=XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_M(datafile,phases)

These operations parse the DAT locally.

docs.title: Read parameters
docs.text:
Use GET functions to retrieve stored H298/S298/Cp data, stoichiometry, molar masses and interaction parameters. Range and coefficient indices are 1-based in the Excel interface.

When a requested numeric datum is structurally unavailable, some GET operations return NaN; an invalid entity/domain can instead produce a clear DAT error. Do not treat NaN as zero.

docs.title: Edit parameters
docs.text:
SET functions modify the selected DAT file itself. Keep a backup before experimentation.

Example pattern:

=XLL_CA_SET_COMPOUND_H298(datafile,phase_names,new_values,update_token)

Successful writes are planned semantically, validated, written to a temporary file and atomically replace the original path.

docs.title: Interaction identity
docs.text: Use XLL_CA_LIST_INTERACTIONS_G/M to obtain the interaction descriptions expected by the interaction GET/SET functions. Do not type or reconstruct interaction identifiers manually if you can reference the spilled list. PyroApp preserves multi-digit interaction powers from the DAT model and does not depend on TQLPAR display formatting.

docs.title: Recalculation after edits
docs.text: A SET formula changes the file, but Excel does not inherently know that another formula's text-path dependency has changed. Use a shared update_token cell to coordinate recalculation when building an editing workbook.

docs.title: Tutorial: first equilibrium table
docs.text:
This example shows the shape of a PyroApp calculation. Use component and phase names from your own datafile.

Assume B1 contains the datafile path.

docs.title: 1. Discover component names
docs.text:
=XLL_CA_LIST_COMPONENTS($B$1)

Use the returned component names exactly in the calculation header.

docs.title: 2. Build the input header
docs.text:
Create a 3-row header with columns for temperature, pressure and incoming component amounts. For a hypothetical two-component system A-B:

B C D E row 1 T, [C] P IA IA row 2 ="" ="" ="" ="" row 3 ="" ="" A B

The third row identifies the system component for the amount columns. Where a phase or constituent/component does not apply, enter ="" so the cell contains the empty-string value rather than being physically blank. This keeps the three-row header contiguous and easy to select and manipulate.

docs.title: 3. Enter calculation points
docs.text: Below the header, enter one row per equilibrium point, for example temperatures and compositions. Use pressure in the default unit (bar) unless the header requests another unit.

docs.title: 4. Build an output header
docs.text:
For example:

G H I row 1 T, [C] A A row 2 ="" LIQUID SOLID row 3 ="" ="" =""

Replace LIQUID and SOLID with real phase names from XLL_CA_LIST_PHASES. Do not leave unused phase or constituent/component header cells physically empty; use ="".

docs.title: 5. Calculate
docs.text:
If the input header is B4:E6, data are B7:E26, and output header is G4:I6:

=XLL_CA_CALCULATE($B$1,B4:E6,B7:E26,G4:I6)

The result spills to 20 rows and 3 columns.

Tip

Prefer one table call with many rows over hundreds of independent one-row formulas. It reduces setup overhead and gives the runtime more opportunity to schedule work efficiently.

docs.title: Tutorial: phase selection
docs.text: Phase selection controls which phases ChemApp may use in a calculation.

docs.title: Base selection with entered
docs.text:
The fifth argument of XLL_CA_CALCULATE is optional. A simple one-row range of phase names defines an entered list.

Conceptually:

=XLL_CA_CALCULATE(datafile,input_header,input,output_header,entered_range)

If one or more phases are explicitly entered, PyroApp first treats the other phases as eliminated and then applies the selected states.

For a richer selection, use a multi-row block with phase names and status prefixes:

  • EN — entered
  • D — dormant
  • EL — eliminated

docs.title: Change selection by calculation row
docs.text:
Add input columns whose row-1 codes are ENTERED, DORMANT or ELIMINATED. The input cell for each point contains a phase name. These row-local controls are applied after the base selection.

This is useful when one table explores several metastable restrictions without creating separate formulas.

docs.title: Isolation between rows
docs.text: PyroApp restores the datafile/base phase state at the beginning of every accepted calculation row. A phase eliminated in row 1 is not accidentally left eliminated in row 2 merely because row 2 leaves the control cell blank.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text: Start with XLL_CA_LIST_PHASES(datafile) to verify spelling. If a row gives an unexpected equilibrium, add ERROR, phase amounts, and relevant activities to the output header before changing the selection logic.

docs.title: Tutorial: remote gRPC calculations
docs.text: Remote mode lets Excel send XLL_CA_CALCULATE jobs to a machine that owns a pool of ChemApp workers.

docs.title: Select the server
docs.text:
In the PyroApp Ribbon tab, select Remote (gRPC) in Connection, enter http://server-name:50051, use Test Connection, then click Apply.

Confirm:

=XLL_PYROAPP_TRANSPORT()

docs.title: What is sent
docs.text:
For a remote XLL_CA_CALCULATE, PyroApp identifies the current datafile by content and format. If that exact version is not already in the server's temporary cache, it uploads the file. The server validates the synchronized copy and gives workers a server-local path.

Changing the file creates a new content identity. Reusing an unchanged file normally avoids a second upload.

docs.title: What is not sent
docs.text:
The local DAT functions remain local:

  • XLL_CA_LIST_*
  • XLL_CA_GET_*
  • XLL_CA_SET_*
  • DAT-based XLL_CA_DIMENSIONS

Changing the transport to gRPC does not turn these into remote database operations.

docs.title: Cache lifetime
docs.text: The current server has an inactivity-based temporary cache policy configured by its operator. Active calculations retain a lease so cleanup cannot remove the file while a worker is using it.

docs.title: Multiple workers
docs.text: The server queues work onto isolated ChemApp processes. Calculation rows can be strongly uneven in execution time, so the architecture favors dynamic assignment of independent work and always restores the original row order in the returned Excel matrix.

docs.title: If the server is unreachable
docs.text:
Switch back to Local (IPC) in the PyroApp Ribbon if you have a local licensed runtime, then click Apply.

Otherwise contact the server operator. PyroApp does not automatically route a failed remote request to a different unconfigured server.

docs.title: Tutorial: target calculations
docs.text: A target calculation solves for a variable that makes a requested thermodynamic condition true. A common example is finding the temperature at which a phase appears.

docs.title: Formation target
docs.text:
Add an input column with FORMATION in header row 1. The input cell contains the phase name whose formation boundary you want to locate.

By default PyroApp solves for temperature. Use VARIABLE only when a different supported target variable is required.

docs.title: Precipitation target
docs.text: PRECIPITATION similarly defines a phase-appearance target using PyroApp's precipitation convention.

docs.title: Direct property targets
docs.text:
The following input codes also activate target solving when used as target conditions:

A, CP, H, S, G, V, AT, XP, XPT.

docs.title: Choose the target variable
docs.text:
A VARIABLE column accepts:

T
P
V
IA
IA0

Temperature is the default.

docs.title: Restrict the search
docs.text:
Use matching limit columns:

  • TLOW, THIGH
  • PLOW, PHIGH
  • VLOW, VHIGH

Good physical bounds can make a target calculation more robust and avoid an irrelevant solution region.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Request the solved variable itself (for example T) plus the relevant phase amount/activity and an ERROR column. This makes the target result auditable rather than returning only a temperature with no indication of solver status.

Warning

A target condition does not guarantee that a physically meaningful solution exists within the chosen search interval. Treat failed target rows as calculation failures, not as missing spreadsheet values to be silently interpolated.
